rationale: Two open limitations of the current account are directly testable with the same scenario: whether an invocation issued with a context that never expires stays pending, and whether a still-pending invocation is admitted once an observed leader change re-arms the run loop's gate (and whether its payload then commits). A native dry run of the corrected harness suggested yes for all three, so a successor experiment is submitted for retained evidence. This batch also answers the four follow-up gaps registered by the knowledge-1 correction: they concern whether that premise correction changes the evidence or conclusions of its recorded uses.

experiment.revision_reason: Prefix change: the removal now goes through joint consensus with automatic leave (ConfChangeV2 with Transition JointImplicit carrying remove node 3) instead of a simple ConfChange, so the member is dropped from both halves only when raft itself leaves the joint state. The harness records that transition as removal_applied (transition joint_implicit, voter false, outgoing false, and the count of applied conf-change entries carrying the removal), and that event is added as a prerequisite of the witness admission, so the witness comparisons now rest on a joint-consensus removal rather than on a simple one. All invocation cases, deadlines, windows, operation ids and expected outcomes are unchanged from the predecessor.

scope.description: Three real raft nodes (ids 1,2,3) driven through the async Node API in one process. Node 1 campaigns and becomes leader in the initial configuration {1,2,3} supplied by the storage ConfState; committed remove-3 and add-3 conf changes are proposed on the leader and applied on every node. Then the experiment issues, on re-added node 3: the witness invocation (2500 ms context), an invocation with a context that never expires (observed for 2000 ms), and two retry attempts (900 ms contexts) each paired with a proposal by never-removed node 2 committed in the same interval; it also runs the control on node 2, then forces a leader change to node 2 at term 2 and issues a further invocation on node 3, and finally observes whether the context-free invocation was admitted by the re-armed gate and whether its payload committed. Every invocation records whether it returned, the error, elapsed time, the node's observed voter status and leader, and whether the payload reached any node's committed entries.
assumptions: Message delivery between the three in-process nodes is reliable and ordered per sender; no ticks are delivered, so leader 1 stays stable until the experiment forces the leader change.
Storage appends of Ready.Entries happen before the Ready's messages are dispatched.

The removal and re-addition are the committed conf changes the driver applies; node 3 applies both through Node.ApplyConfChange. The context-free invocation is issued before any leader change and is not cancelled by the harness, so its admission can only come from the run loop re-arming its receive side.
excluded: RawNode.Propose (no gate exists on that path)
Network faults: delivery is reliable, so non-delivery cannot be attributed to message loss
Node stop as a release path for the context-free invocation (the harness no longer stops the node mid-scenario)

experiment.prefix: Start nodes 1,2,3 with a MemoryStorage per node whose ConfState voters are {1,2,3} (captured test helper withPeers). Node 1 campaigns at term 1 and becomes leader; every node then reports leader 1 and node 1 has applied the initial entry. Propose a remove-3 ConfChange on node 1 and wait until node 3's applied entries contain it and node 3's configuration excludes node 3 (voter=false). Propose an add-3 ConfChange on node 1 and wait until node 3's applied entries contain it and node 3's configuration includes node 3 again (voter=true) with leader still 1. Then run the witness invocation, the context-free invocation, the control, the two retry/progress intervals, and the forced leader change with the final invocation and the post-re-arm observations on node 3.
experiment.responsibility: Client-facing obligation of the Node interface: a Propose invocation on a voting member whose leader is known must either reach a proposal outcome (appended locally or forwarded to the leader) or return an error to the caller, within an interval the caller can bound; a context-free invocation must not be silently held until an unrelated leadership change admits it.

interpretations.joint_history: All three receipts run the same fixed scenario lineage: 3592ccaf01864f56aaf06d54a3f97423-experiment (executed as 43a04622beef40588679c6cf1c40d6ad) and its successors 48ce57b251a644edaaf9d17731df0b25-experiment (a9f71d7a07454d058d818148f7479e8f) and baee4030bf1e4f229c46ece8d0ddc365-experiment (87b38a551d554c2391427dda00c4e6e4), each registered with previous_id and a revision_reason. All three build the same configuration {1,2,3} from the same storage ConfState, elect leader 1 at term 1, apply the same committed remove-3 and add-3 conf changes on node 3, use the same witness/control/repair operation ids, payloads, phases, deadlines and windows, and force the same campaign of node 2 into term 2; the successors change event naming and then add retry/progress cases without altering the earlier ones. Witnesses agree field for field at the corresponding indices (witness 7/8/9 in all three; control 11/12; repair 15/16 or 25/26), so the difference is a property of the fixed scenario rather than of one run.
interpretations.rationale: Mechanism statement corrected in the previous revision; evidence unchanged. In 87b38a551d554c2391427dda00c4e6e4, node 3 applied its own re-admission (index 4) and its configuration listed it as a voter with leader 1 (index 5); the admitted invocation (index 6) had not returned after 1200 ms (index 7), released only at the caller's deadline (index 8: 'context deadline exceeded', 2501 ms), and left its payload absent from every node's committed entries (index 9). During the same stable-leader period the never-removed member's invocation returned in 0 ms and committed on all three nodes (indices 11, 12); two independent retries on node 3 (indices 14, 19) also never completed and were not committed, while in each interval a fresh proposal by node 2 returned in 0 ms and committed on all three nodes (indices 17, 22); after the leader change 1->2 at term 2 (index 23) a new invocation on node 3 returned in 0 ms and committed (indices 25, 26). Source account: the run loop's gate variable is assigned only at node.go:374/377/426 and used as the receive case at node.go:386, and a re-admission cannot match the removal guard because the local Progress entry is already gone (node.go:401-412), so the caller's send on n.propc (node.go:525) stays pending while no leader change is observed. The snapshot's own expectation (node_test.go:352-385) scopes intended blocking to a node that does not know the current leader, which is not this case; the control and interval controls exclude cluster-wide stalls, and the post-leader-change call excludes a defect in node 3's state machine. Net effect: a member's proposal duty is held pending without any error signal for as long as no leader change is observed, and the successor experiment submitted in this batch tests whether that pending duty is admitted by a later leader change and whether the unbounded case stays pending.
counterevidence: node.go:407-411 acknowledges the gate as improvised ('propc is reset when the leader changes ... This isn't very sound and likely has bugs'); this explains the dependence on leader changes but is neither a calling restriction nor a protection, and no other re-arm path exists in the snapshot.

node_test.go:352-385 shows that not returning is intended for a node that does not know the current leader. That expectation does not cover the witnessed case, and the same test expects acceptance once a leader is known.

The pending invocation is not lost: it is admitted unmodified when the gate is re-armed (node.go:386 resumes receiving from n.propc), so the harmed interval is 'no observed leader change', not the entire lifetime of the node.
The same run contains successful paths (indices 12, 17, 22, 26), showing proposals are neither generally dropped nor generally blocked.
limitations: Comparison outcomes for the earliest receipt were 'unknown' because that harness gave the three operations' result events the same names; its decisive events are complete and match the successor receipts, which have complete holds.

Scope is the async Node API path (node.run loop) in this snapshot; RawNode.Propose has no such gate. No ticks were delivered and delivery was reliable, so no timing or network-fault characterization is claimed.

Only the voter-removal form was executed; other transitions that delete the local Progress entry are variants of the same cause and were not executed separately. The same gate also covers Node.ProposeConfChange (node.go:496-502 via stepWithWaitOption), which was not executed.

The context-free invocation and the admission of a still-pending invocation by a later leader change are established from source and seen in a native dry run only; the successor experiment submitted in this batch is the retained test for both, so until its receipt exists these two remain outside the retained evidence.
